THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:832  WP No. 108611 of 2019  C/W WP No. 108610 of 2019  ORDER
These petitions are filed by the Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

Challenging the order passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Athani in Execution Case Nos.25 and 26 of 2017 by which attachment warrant of movables was reissued against the petitioners herein.

2. On the claim petitions filed by the respondents herein, the Fast Track, Athani had awarded a compensation amount of Rs.3,96,000/- to the claimants in MVC No.1050/2012 and a compensation amount of Rs.1,72,500/- to the claimants in MVC No.1051/2012 with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization of the entire compensation amount.
3. The petitioner challenged the award passed by the Trial Court before this Court in MFA Nos.22714 and 22715 of 2013.
At the time of filing the appeal, the petitioner had deposited this statutory amount of Rs.25,000/- each before this Court.
This Court granted an interim order of stay subject to the condition, the petitioner deposits 50% of the award amount.
In the light of the interim order granted by this Court, the petitioner deposited 50% of the award amount before the Trial Court including the amount of Rs.25,000/- deposited before this Court.

4. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the Trial Court has erroneously calculated the interest on the amount which was deposited by the petitioner in the light of the interim order granted by this Court and the NC: 2024:KHC-D:832 petitioner having deposited the said amount is not liable to pay interest on the said amount from the date on which the interim order was granted till disposal of the appeal.

5. Learned counsel for the respondents - claimants submitted that though the amount was deposited in the light of the interim order granted by this Court, however, the claimants have not withdrawn the amount and as such, they are entitled for interest from the date on which the interim order was granted till the disposal of the appeal.

6. The issue as to whether the liability of the insurance company to pay interest gets discharged when it deposits the award amount was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.Kala Bharathi and others vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, Branch Chitoor reported in (2014) 5 SCC 577.

6. At paragraphs 14, 15, 25 and 26 are held as under:
"14.

A bare perusal of the aforesaid provisions makes it amply clear that the scope of Order XXI Rule 1 of the CPC is that the judgment debtor is required to pay the The Divisional Manager vs Smt.Kamalavva W/O Basappa Kamble on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195736239/
3 decretal amount in one of the modes specified in sub- rule (1) thereof.

sentences.text: Sub-rule (2) of Rule 1 provides that once payment is made under sub-rule (1), it is the duty of the judgment debtor to give notice to the decree-holder through the Court or directly to him by registered post acknowledgement due.

Sub-rule (3) of Rule 1 merely indicates that in case money is paid by postal money order or through a bank under clause (a)
or clause (b) of sub-rule (1) thereof, certain particulars are required to be accurately incorporated while making such payment.
Sub- rules (4) and (5) of Rule 1 states from which date, interest shall cease to run in case amount is paid under clause (a) or (c) of sub- rule (1), - V. Kala Bharathi & Ors vs The Oriental ...

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: on 1 April, 2014 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83910908/ 5 interest shall NC:

2024 :KHC-D:832 cease to run from the date of service of notice as indicated under sub-rule (2); while in case of out of court payment to the decree- holder by way of any of the modes mentioned under clause (b) of sub-rule (1), interest shall cease to run from the date of such payment.

15. The language contained in the aforesaid sub- rules clearly indicates the appropriation of amount to be made in case the decree contains a specific clause,
specifying the manner in which the money deposited to be appropriated.
Sub-rule (1)(c) of Rule 1 indicates the money deposited to be appropriated as per the direction of the Court, if there is a provision in that behalf.
In the absence of specific direction with regard to appropriation, then only the manner of appropriation would arise for consideration.

Sub-rules (2) to (5) of Rule 1 indicate the procedure to be followed when the deposit is made either under clause (a) or (b) of sub-rule (1) thereof, but it does not leave any scope for interpretation with regard to appropriation of deposited amount by the decree-holder.
25.
The next finding of the High Court is with regard to interest on interest.
In money suit, the amount consists of principal and interest till the suit is filed.
But, in case of award passed under the Act, the question of inclusion of any interest on the decretal amount does not arise.
Unfortunately, the High Court proceeded on the assumption that it amounts to interest on interest which is prohibited under Section 3(3)(c) of Interest Act, 1978 (for short, the Interest Act).

This is not so, as in the facts and circumstances of the present case, the decree passed by the trial Court or the appellate Court does not contain the mode of appropriation and in the absence of any such direction, the decree-holder is entitled to appropriate the amount deposited by the judgment debtor first towards interest, then cost and thereafter towards principal.

26. In view of above and more particularly keeping in view the ratio of the Constitution Bench judgment in Gurpreet Singh (supra), where considering an identical question in respect of Order XXI Rule 1 of the CPC, it was held that if the amount deposited by the judgment debtor falls short of the decretal amount, the decree-holder is entitled to apply the rule of appropriation by appropriating the amount first towards interest, then towards costs and subsequently towards principal The Divisional Manager vs Smt.Kamalavva W/O Basappa Kamble on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195736239/

sentences.text: 4 amount due under the decree; we are of the opinion that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:832 appellants herein are entitled to the amount awarded by the Executing Court, as the amounts deposited by the judgment debtor fell short of the decretal amount.
After such appropriation, the decree-holder is entitled to interest only to the extent of unpaid principal amount.

Hence, interest be calculated on the unpaid principal amount."
7.

The arrest warrant having been issued, the petitioner deposited the entire compensation amount of Rs.4,04,171/- with accrued interest excluding the statutory deposit of Rs.25,000/- on 10.10.2013 and a sum of Rs.1,62,302/- excluding the statutory deposit of Rs.25,000/- on 10.10.2013.
This Court vide order dated 11.10.2013 stayed the execution of the award, which was impugned by the petitioner subject to deposit of 50% of the award amount.
Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application before the Execution Court to disburse the compensation amount deposited.
In view of the objection raised, the compensation amount was not disbursed to the claimant.
The appeals ultimately came to be dismissed on 14.9.2016 confirming the award passed by the Trial Court.

Admittedly, the amount deposited by the petitioner was not disbursed to the claimant in view of the objections filed by the petitioner and also the interim order granted by this Court in the aforesaid appeals.
8. Order 21 Rule (4) states that on any amount paid under clause (a) or clause (c) of sub-rule (1)
interest, if any, shall cease to run from the date of service of the notice referred to in sub-rule (2).

Sub-Rule (5) states that on any amount paid under clause (b) of sub-rule (1), interest, if any, NC:
2024:KHC-D:832 shall cease to run from the date of such payment.

In the instant case, admittedly,
there is no payment of compensation by the Insurance Company to the claimants.

However, the Insurance Company has only deposited the decretal amount with interest, but however, objected for disbursal of the said amount to the claimants and based on the said objection, the claimants were deprived of the amount to which, they were entitled under the award and they cannot be deprived of the interest on the compensation amount from the date on which this Court granted the interim order till disposal of the appeal.
Further, this Court had granted the interim order without reserving liberty to the claimants to withdraw the amount to be deposited by the Insurance Company.

Therefore, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the interest on the amount deposited by it from 10.10.2013 till disposal of the appeal i.e. 14.9.2016.
9.

The Co-Ordinate bench of this Court in W.P. No.201824/2023 at paragraph No.8 has held as follows:
"Whenever any judgment or award is passed in favour of a party, be it a claimant or a plaintiff such party would be entitled for the principal amount and interest thereon till the date of receipt of the amounts.

Merely because, the defendant or the judgment debtor were to deposit the amounts in a Court of law or as done in this case before the Workmen's Compensation Commissioner, the obligation to pay the amounts would not cease.

What is of relevance is for the claimant or plaintiff to receive the monies which have been ordered in his or her favour, the deposit of the money not enure to the benefit of the plaintiff/claimant thereby depriving him of the beneficial The Divisional Manager vs Smt.Kamalavva W/O Basappa Kamble on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195736239/
5 use of the money, such deprivation being as a result of a judgment debtor or the NC:
2024:KHC-D:832 petitioner in the present case not releasing money in favour of the claimant/decree holder/plaintiff."
10.

Accordingly, the petitions stand disposed off.
